correctness.rationale: For residuals P=X−x, Q=Y−y, differentiate P(f(y),y)=Q(g(y),y)=0 to get det(I−J)=det D(P,Q)=P_x Q_x(f′−g′). At an interior equilibrium P_x=−rx, Q_x=y/x, giving the factor −ry. H(0+)=1−1/(βb)<0 and every positive-y zero is an interior equilibrium because g(y)>0. At the first such zero H′≥0, with strict inequality if transverse. Hence p(1)=det(I−J)≤0 excludes strict Schur stability; at equality 1 is a multiplier, while strict negativity puts a real characteristic root above 1. The stated rx≤2 saddle test additionally requires transversality: writing A=βbxS(1+2cy)>0 and B=by e^{r(1−x)}S(1+2cy)>0, p(−1)=(2−rx)(1+A)+B>0, locating the other root strictly between −1 and 1. The displayed rx≤2 is a sufficient cutoff, not an iff threshold; no nonlinear conclusion follows just from H′=0. A fresh bisection/Jacobian reproduction (lower_equilibrium_reproduction.py with its output in the private numerical evidence; the frozen verification/verify.py was only inspected) agreed with the determinant test and gave multipliers 0.010601260510 and 1.019517400112 at r=1, and −1.994045049924 and 1.019721561378 at r=3, with (β,b,c)=(2,0.49,3). Those bounded checks reproduce the local examples, not a global root count. The analytic statement is conditional on exactly two positive equilibria and does not establish that hypothesis for arbitrary parameters.

evidence: The same-map count theorem gives an at-most-two bound and a strict maximum for the scalar equilibrium equation; it explicitly does not classify branch stability. Its increasing lower branch can in fact supply the crossing direction in its two-root regime, but not the Jacobian sign test by itself.

The other indexed cooperation threshold is a different Beverton–Holt-type map; the closest cited predation analogues have different recruitment/refuge mechanisms. The cited Taylor & Francis DOI routes did not give full texts.

originality.rationale: The planar nullcline determinant identity is general and not itself new. The strongest same-map indexed overlap reports a separate result on instability of a lower equilibrium under the same two-equilibrium assumption, without naming or giving that result. This could refer to the frozen finding itself; it is evidence of overlap in the instability claim, not evidence of a distinct earlier theorem covering the model-specific Jury conclusion including the explicit saddle cutoff. Credit the supported joint refinement for this exact model, not novelty of the determinant technique or proof of priority for the lower-instability observation alone.
